strings.d1.s0.name: Nevsky Prospekt
strings.d1.s0.tips: A 4.5 km main boulevard. Look for the Kazan Cathedral colonnade and the Singer building (Dom Knigi bookshop).
strings.d1.s1.name: Kazan Cathedral
strings.d1.s1.tips: Colonnade reminiscent of St Peter's. Free entry, with Kutuzov's tomb inside.
strings.d1.s2.name: Church of the Savior on Spilled Blood
strings.d1.s2.tips: Russian-style church with 7,000 m² of mosaics, on the spot where Alexander II was assassinated. Closed Wednesday; buy tickets online.
strings.d1.s3.name: Pyshechnaya Bolshaya Konyushennaya
strings.d1.s3.tips: A Soviet-era pyshki (ring doughnut) shop open since 1958. Expect a queue; cash only.
strings.d1.s4.name: Russian Museum
strings.d1.s4.tips: The largest collection of Russian art, including Repin and Aivazovsky's The Ninth Wave. Closed Tuesday.
strings.d1.b0.name: Stolle Pirogi Nevsky
strings.d1.b0.tips: Russian pies (pirogi). A chain, but a good one.
strings.d1.b1.name: Griboyedov Canal behind Kazan Cathedral
strings.d1.b1.tips: A walk along the canal bank, in place of the garden.
strings.d2.s0.name: Palace Square
strings.d2.s0.tips: The Alexander Column and the General Staff arch, in front of the Winter Palace.
strings.d2.s1.name: State Hermitage Museum
strings.d2.s1.tips: The Winter Palace and 3 million works: Rembrandt, Da Vinci, the Raphael Loggias, and the Peacock Clock at 12:00. Book a timed ticket online; closed Monday; allow 4 hours.
strings.d2.s2.name: Hermitage Cafeteria
strings.d2.s2.tips: The cafeteria inside the museum: a quick lunch without leaving.
strings.d2.s3.name: General Staff Building Hermitage
strings.d2.s3.tips: Impressionists (Monet, Matisse, Picasso), across the square. Combined ticket 1,400.
strings.d2.s4.name: Admiralty Embankment
strings.d2.s4.tips: A stroll along the Neva with views of the Bronze Horseman and the Isaac's dome.
strings.d2.b0.name: Teremok Nevsky
strings.d2.b0.tips: A blini (crepe) chain: cheap and fast.
strings.d2.b1.name: Winter Palace of Peter I
strings.d2.b1.tips: Remains of Peter's first palace, as an alternative to the General Staff Building.
strings.d3.s0.name: Peterhof Lower Park
strings.d3.s0.tips: Take the Meteor hydrofoil (35 minutes, 2,000 RUB) or a minibus. The Grand Cascade opens at 11:00, with 150 fountains and trick fountains (May to October).
strings.d3.s1.name: Peterhof Grand Palace
strings.d3.s1.tips: Rastrelli's gilded halls. Timed tickets; closed Monday.
strings.d3.s2.name: Shtandart Restaurant Peterhof
strings.d3.s2.tips: A Russian restaurant next to the park, serving borscht and pelmeni.
strings.d3.s3.name: Alexandria Park Peterhof
strings.d3.s3.tips: The neighbouring park, with the Cottage Palace and the Gulf shoreline.
strings.d3.b0.name: Peterhof Bolshoy Cafe
strings.d3.b0.tips: A cheap cafe in the town.
strings.d3.b1.name: Monplaisir Palace
strings.d3.b1.tips: Peter's seaside pavilion, as an alternative to Alexandria.
strings.d4.s0.name: Peter and Paul Fortress
strings.d4.s0.tips: The island where the city was born. The cathedral holds the Romanov tombs, there is a cannon shot at 12:00, and the beach has city views.
strings.d4.s1.name: Petrovsky Cafe Fortress
strings.d4.s1.tips: A cafe inside the fortress, for lunch.
strings.d4.s2.name: Rostral Columns Strelka
strings.d4.s2.tips: The tip of Vasilyevsky Island: the columns and a panorama of the Neva.
strings.d4.s3.name: Kunstkamera
strings.d4.s3.tips: Peter's 1714 cabinet of curiosities. Closed Monday.
strings.d4.s4.name: Vasilyevsky Lines Walk
strings.d4.s4.tips: Streets known as numbered 'liniya' lines, and the Andreyevsky market.
strings.d4.b0.name: Erarta Museum
strings.d4.b0.tips: Contemporary Russian art on Vasilyevsky, instead of the Kunstkamera.
strings.d4.b1.name: Marketplace Vasilyevsky
strings.d5.s0.name: Catherine Palace
strings.d5.s0.tips: 45 minutes by train and bus or by taxi (Tsarskoye Selo). See the Amber Room and the Great Hall. Timed tickets sell out online.
strings.d5.s1.name: Catherine Park
strings.d5.s1.tips: A lake, the Cameron Gallery and pavilions. Boats in summer.
strings.d5.s2.name: Podvorye Restaurant Pushkin
strings.d5.s2.tips: Decorated like a Russian village house, and a restaurant Putin has eaten at. Blini and meat dishes.
strings.d5.s3.name: Alexander Palace
strings.d5.s3.tips: The last Tsar's home, with restored private rooms.
strings.d5.b0.name: Pavlovsk Palace
strings.d5.b0.tips: The neighbouring Pavlovsk palace and its vast park, instead of Alexander Palace.
strings.d5.b1.name: Beliy Medved Cafe Pushkin
strings.d5.b1.tips: Good value in the town centre.
strings.d6.s0.name: Saint Isaac's Cathedral
strings.d6.s0.tips: A huge golden dome. The colonnade has 262 steps (extra charge) and a city panorama. Closed Wednesday.
strings.d6.s1.name: Bronze Horseman
strings.d6.s1.tips: The statue of Peter the Great on Senate Square.
strings.d6.s2.name: Yusupov Palace
strings.d6.s2.tips: The palace where Rasputin was killed, with a home theatre and the cellar scene. Audio guide available.
strings.d6.s3.name: Sadko Restaurant Mariinsky
strings.d6.s3.tips: Russian food next to the Mariinsky: a classic before the theatre.
strings.d6.s4.name: Neva and Canal Boat Tour
strings.d6.s4.tips: A White Nights canal tour. The bridges open at 01:10 (Palace Bridge); the route runs along the Fontanka and Moyka.
strings.d6.b0.name: Mariinsky Theatre
strings.d6.b0.tips: A ballet or opera evening. Book online weeks ahead (prices are higher for tourists).
strings.d6.b1.name: Marketplace Isaac
strings.d7.s0.name: Summer Garden
strings.d7.s0.tips: Peter's garden from 1704, with statues and fountains (May to October). Closed Monday.
strings.d7.s1.name: Fabergé Museum
strings.d7.s1.tips: Nine imperial eggs in the Shuvalov Palace, on the Fontanka.
strings.d7.s2.name: Yeliseyev Emporium
strings.d7.s2.tips: A luxury art nouveau grocery from 1903. Cakes and champagne at the cafe corner, plus gifts.
strings.d7.s3.name: Moskovsky Vokzal / Pulkovo Bus
strings.d7.s3.tips: To the airport: metro to Moskovskaya, then bus 39, 60 minutes. Farewell.
strings.d7.b0.name: Cafe Singer Dom Knigi
strings.d7.b0.tips: A bookshop cafe with a view of Kazan Cathedral.
strings.d7.b1.name: Anna Akhmatova Museum
strings.d7.b1.tips: The poet's apartment in the Fountain House, instead of Fabergé.
strings.note0: Metro token or Podorozhnik card (about 70 RUB); the metro is deep. Pulkovo Airport: metro to Moskovskaya, then bus 39. For taxis, use the Yandex Go app.
strings.note1: White Nights run from late May to mid-July (twilight at 01:00). The bridges open from 01:10 to 05:00, so choose your accommodation on the right side of the Neva. Summer is 20-25°C; bring a raincoat.
strings.note2: Visa: Turkish citizens get 60 days visa-free; others can use an e-visa. Visa/Mastercard do NOT work (since 2022): bring cash RUB or use Mir/UnionPay. A Turkish Ziraat card sometimes works, but bring cash.
strings.note3: Hermitage 1,000 RUB (timed, online), Catherine Palace 2,200, Peterhof park 1,500 + palace 2,000, Spilled Blood 550. Closed days: Monday for the Hermitage and Peterhof, Wednesday for Spilled Blood and Isaac's, Tuesday for the Russian Museum.
strings.note4: Borscht, pelmeni, blini, pyshki. Business lunch (biznes-lanch) 12:00-16:00 about 500 RUB; tip 10%.
strings.note5: Keep your passport on you; hotels handle registration (registratsiya). Yandex Maps is more accurate than Google Maps.
